Starts tracking a budget on a project you already have. A project has at most one budget, so creating a second one returns `422`.

`calculation_mode` sets the unit of every number in the budget: `fee` counts money in the project's currency, `time` counts hours. `amount` is a plain decimal in that unit, not cents — `"5000"` on a `fee` budget is 5,000.00 and `"37.5"` on a `time` budget is 37.5 hours.

`calculation_base` has to be one the mode can count, and any other is rejected:

| `calculation_mode` | `calculation_base` |
| --- | --- |
| `fee` | `billable_time`, `billable_time_and_expenses`, `expenses` |
| `time` | `billable_time`, `non_billable_time`, `billable_and_non_billable_time` |

Every setting you leave out is taken from the company's budget settings in Bonsai, the ones the app pre-fills. A default `calculation_base` the mode cannot count becomes `billable_time`.

The project needs a `start_date`, because budget cycles run from it; set one with `PATCH /public-api/v1/projects/{id}` first. A project that starts in the future gets its budget right away, and its first cycle opens on the start date.

A project the token cannot see returns `404`. One it can see returns `403` when the token may not change the project or see its budget, or when the plan does not include budgets.
